blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Customer e-mail address written to the error log on a failed lookup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Phone, birth date, address and e-mail sent to the Helply chat vendor when only the name is needed) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (e.g. `throw new NotFoundError("no customer with this e-mail")`). Every lookup of an unknown address reaches `errorHandler` in src/server.ts, which runs `logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`, so the typed address — personal data, and possibly a third person's address mistyped by the agent — lands in the application logs with no retention rule tied to it (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 32). Add a test that a not-found lookup logs no e-mail address.
findings.title: Customer e-mail address written to the error log on a failed lookup

findings.evidence:
user: {
  id: String(customer.id),
  name: customer.name,
  email: customer.email,
  phone: customer.phone,
  birthDate: customer.birth_date,
  address: customer.address,
},
findings.recommendation: The proposal's purpose is that the widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to"; send only `id` and `name` to Helply (an opaque id lets the agent use the support lookup for the rest). Every signed-in customer who opens the chat today has their phone number, birth date, postal address and e-mail address handed to a third-party processor beyond what the purpose needs (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25, Art. 28). Also select only the needed columns in `customerById` for this route.
findings.title: Phone, birth date, address and e-mail sent to the Helply chat vendor when only the name is needed

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The proposal states agents look a customer up so they stop asking "who they are"; returning the full record (birth date, phone, postal address) to every agent with the `support` role goes beyond identification unless the team states why agents need each field. Confirm which fields the support screen uses and return only those (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)).
findings.title: Support lookup returns birth date, phone and postal address the identification purpose may not need

findings.recommendation: Question for the team — the change starts sharing customer data with Helply, but the plan does not state the lawful basis, that a processor agreement (GDPR Art. 28) is in place, nor whether Helply transfers data outside the EEA (Chapter V). Record it in the proposal or a decision; only the controller can answer.
findings.title: Helply not identified as a processor, nor its hosting location
